structured_output.hypothesis: Oceanic (never land-connected) islands hold fewer vascular plant species than mainland regions of equal area, and the shortfall remains after accounting for climate and habitat heterogeneity.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Fit log10(species richness) ~ log10(area) + island-type (oceanic island vs mainland) on GIFT regions, using only regions of 100–100,000 km² that have complete native vascular-plant checklists. Then add mean annual temperature, annual precipitation and elevational range as covariates. The claim passes if the oceanic-island coefficient is negative with a 95% CI wholly below 0 in both models. In addition, the area-matched median richness ratio (oceanic island / mainland, in 0.25 log10-area bins) must be ≤0.5 in at least 75% of bins that contain ≥5 regions of each type. This tests the 'far fewer' wording and the 'not explained by physical conditions' clause.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if the oceanic-island coefficient in either model is non-negative or has a 95% CI that includes 0. It also fails if the area-matched median richness ratio is >0.5 in more than 25% of eligible bins. If the covariates make the island effect vanish (CI includes 0), the 'not explained by physical conditions' clause is refuted.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Species of all kinds' is operationalised as native vascular plant species, the most completely inventoried group in GIFT. 'Oceanic islands' means islands never connected to a continent, classified from GIFT's island-geology fields (oceanic = volcanic or atoll origin, excluding continental fragments and land-bridge islands). 'Equal continental areas' means mainland regions of the same area, matched by log-area bins or regressed on log area. 'Physical conditions' is modernised to climate (temperature, precipitation) and topographic relief, taken from GIFT's environmental layers. Only native species are counted, so introductions do not mask the difference. This is a modern reinterpretation: Darwin's phrase was qualitative, and the test is for a quantitative richness deficit. The test uses plants only. Animal groups would need a separate dataset.

dataset.name: GIFT – Global Inventory of Floras and Traits
dataset.publisher: Biodiversity, Macroecology & Biogeography group, University of Göttingen (Weigelt, Kreft et al.)
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT is a public database of native vascular-plant checklists for more than 2,900 geographic regions, covering both islands and mainland areas. Each region record carries area, island status and geological origin, plus climate and elevation variables. The data are reachable through the web interface and the GIFT R package, which queries the API. The fields used would be: native species richness per checklist or region, area (km²), island/mainland flag, island geology (oceanic vs continental), mean annual temperature, precipitation, and elevation range.
